objections_raised: Wittgenstein's objection to the robust assertoric force of 'I believe p'

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis and comparative philosophical exegesis
named_thought_experiments: Moore's Paradox utterance: 'I believe it is not raining, but as a matter of fact it is raining.'

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Analytic philosophy of language and epistemology
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: The nature of assertion, belief, and rationality

structural_organization.structure_type: Recursive and layered - the abstract is repeated with increasing specificity in each subsequent section (Moore, Grice, Wittgenstein, Synthesis)

summary_of_core_decisions: The text constructs a layered dialectic: (1) Moore's implicative relation establishes the semantic commitment; (2) Grice's pragmatics reframes the absurdity as a violation of conversational maxims; (3) Wittgenstein's use theory challenges the assertoric premise, shifting the analysis to conceptual grammar; (4) The final synthesis concludes that the absurdity primarily violates practical rationality (norms of assertion) rather than theoretical rationality (logical consistency).

thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low - the final claim is definitive regarding the primary violation being practical rationality
